run.question: We're getting mapping errors and slow indexing on our events index. Can you check the field mappings for our app-188-index-* indexes and tell me if any have an unusually high number of fields? What's the exact field count for each?

report.summary: Four indices match the pattern app-188-index-* and all are green and open. Three of them (app-188-index-a, -b, -c) each map exactly 10 top-level fields with the identical field list; app-188-index-x maps 523 top-level fields (655 fields counting typed sub-fields), which is by far the outlier. 520 of those 523 names are four families of 130 numeric-suffixed fields each (counter_*, flag_*, label_*, metric_*), plus @timestamp, event_type and user_id — a shape consistent with dynamic mapping growth, but the mapping errors and slow indexing themselves were not observed in this Run's evidence, so tying them to this index remains a hypothesis.

claims.text: Four indices match app-188-index-*: app-188-index-a, app-188-index-b, app-188-index-c (docs.count 0 each) and app-188-index-x (docs.count 1); all four are health green and status open.

Exact top-level mapping field counts: app-188-index-a = 10, app-188-index-b = 10, app-188-index-c = 10, app-188-index-x = 523. Counting every node that carries a "type" (i.e. including multi-fields), the counts are 10, 10, 10 and 655 for app-188-index-x.
app-188-index-a, app-188-index-b and app-188-index-c have an identical 10-field mapping: @timestamp, action, duration_ms, error_message, event_type, ip_address, metadata, session_id, status, user_id.
The 523 top-level fields of app-188-index-x group by name prefix as: counter_ = 130, flag_ = 130, label_ = 130, metric_ = 130, plus @timestamp, event_type and user_id (1 each).

Sampled rows of the app-188-index-x mapping (first 40 top-level fields returned) show numerically suffixed names such as counter_0001, counter_0005, counter_0009 ... typed as long, with @timestamp typed as date.

app-188-index-x is the index with an unusually high field count (523 top-level, ~52x the others) and its mapping is dominated by generated numeric-suffixed field families, which is consistent with unchecked dynamic mapping growth; this could contribute to the reported mapping errors and slow indexing on that index, but no error log, mapper exception or indexing-latency measurement was retrieved in this Run to confirm it.

Search the Elasticsearch/OpenSearch server logs for the exact error strings (for example mapper_parsing_exception or a total-fields-limit message) on app-188-index-x before changing anything, since the field count alone does not prove the reported mapping errors originate there.

If the numeric-suffixed counter_*, flag_*, label_* and metric_* families are not intentionally queried, consider halting the growth (dynamic templates, flattened or disabled dynamic mapping, or explicit mapping for these event fields) rather than only raising index.mapping.total_fields.limit.

gaps: No Elasticsearch/OpenSearch log line or exception text about mapping errors or slow indexing was retrieved; the reported symptoms are therefore unverified in this evidence set.

The mappings and index list are cluster state observed at 2026-11-21T05:04:54Z (just after the authorized window end 2026-11-21T05:04:51Z); they cannot show what the mappings were earlier in the window or when fields were added.

Index settings that govern field proliferation, such as index.mapping.total_fields.limit and any dynamic templates, were not readable with the available tools, so whether a field limit is being approached or breached is unknown.
Which index the reported mapping errors actually occur on is unknown; app-188-index-a, -b and -c have 0 documents each, so their behavior under indexing was not observed.
The app-188-index-x mapping was sampled only for the first 40 top-level fields; the remaining field names were not individually read (only counted and prefix-grouped).
Change history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so any recent mapping or template change cannot be confirmed.
next_steps: Inspect Elasticsearch/OpenSearch logs and the events index error stream for the exact mapping exception text and the index name it names.
Compare app-188-index-x's field count against index.mapping.total_fields.limit and any dynamic template or component template that would generate counter_*/flag_*/label_*/metric_* fields.
Verify whether app-188-index-a, -b and -c are intended empty (mapping-only) indices or are not receiving writes as expected.

query.jq: to_entries | .[] | {index: .key, top_level_fields: (.value.mappings.properties | keys | length), fields_with_type: ([.value.mappings.properties | .. | objects | select(has("type"))] | length)}

.["app-188-index-x"].mappings.properties | to_entries | map({field: .key, type: (.value.type // (if .value.properties then "object" else "unknown" end)), subfields: ((.value.properties // .value.fields) | if . then keys else [] end)}) | .[0:40]
.["app-188-index-x"].mappings.properties | keys | map(sub("[0-9]+$";"")) | group_by(.) | map({prefix: .[0], count: length}) | sort_by(-.count)
